question.text: Under the SEBI framework for AIF valuation, the Investment Manager must inform investors with reasons if a per-asset-level valuation deviation exceeds specified thresholds. What are the applicable thresholds?

answer.text: More than 15% between consecutive valuations OR more than 25% in a financial year
More than 25% between consecutive valuations OR more than 50% in a financial year
More than 10% between consecutive valuations OR more than 20% in a financial year
More than 20% between consecutive valuations OR more than 33% in a financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: At each asset level, if there is a deviation of more than 20% between two consecutive valuations, OR a deviation of more than 33% in a financial year, the Investment Manager shall inform investors with reasons, including changes in accounting practices, assumptions, projections, methodology, or approach. The Trap: The 10/20 and 15/25 pairs understate the regulatory thresholds. The 25/50 pair is too lax and would suppress disclosures the regulation intends investors to receive. Note: The thresholds apply at the individual asset level — not at the fund-NAV level — and the disclosure must include the underlying reasons, not just the percentage move.
